evals.prompt: Scan security. The users table has a password column stored in clear text. There is no Supabase Auth and no Google, Outlook, or GitHub login.
evals.expected_output: Says sign-in is username and password. Says passwords live in a hand-built schema, in clear text, and says that first. Does not call it Supabase Auth. Does not print a password. Does not change the schema.
assertions: Says sign-in is username and password
Says passwords live in a hand-built schema in clear text
Does not call it Supabase Auth

evals.prompt: People sign in with Supabase Auth. I do not see a password column in our tables. I do not see Google, Outlook, or GitHub.
evals.expected_output: Says passwords live in Supabase Auth, not in a hand-built schema. Says there is no platform provider. Does not call this the mature status.
assertions: Says passwords live in Supabase Auth
Says this is not a hand-built password schema
Says there is no platform provider
Does not call this the mature status

evals.prompt: Sign-in is Google and GitHub. The env has GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET and GITHUB_CLIENT_ID. There is no password column.
evals.expected_output: Says the providers are Google and GitHub, which is the mature status. Names the OAuth settings and does not print the values.
assertions: Says the providers are Google and GitHub

evals.prompt: GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET is in the env. Where should that secret live?
evals.expected_output: Uses the infisical skill. Does not print the secret.
